question.problem:
Let $⟨2,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x+ky=5 \\ x+2y=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

II. $2|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

III. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=2|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$
question.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ 2 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|} \\ 2|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".
